description.value: The study examined how long-term meditation and short-term mindfulness meditation training affect amygdala reactivity and amygdala–VMPFC functional connectivity during emotional picture viewing in healthy adults.

spans.text: The current study investigated a greater range of practice by including long- and short-term practitioners

value: We hypothesized that mindfulness meditation training would decrease reactivity to affective stimuli, as assessed by amygdala activation to positive and negative pictures (relative to neutral).

We further hypothesized that mindfulness meditation training would enhance automatic emotion regulation, as reflected by greater amygdala-VMPFC functional connectivity during affective pictures (negative, positive) relative to neutral.

description.value: The study combined a cross-sectional comparison of long-term meditators and meditation-naïve participants with a randomized controlled trial comparing Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction and the Health Enhancement Program.

spans.text: We employed a rigorous design combining cross-sectional analysis of long-term meditators (LTM) compared to meditation-naïve participants (MNP), and a randomized controlled trial (RCT)
